| `426 desktop_app_outdated` bei der Anmeldung | Die App ist älter als `server.desktop_min_version` oder nennt keine Version. Aktualisiere die App. |

en.title: subkit CLI reference
en.summary: Look up every subkit command and argument here.
en.body:
# subkit CLI reference

Look up every `subkit` command and argument here. Creating or changing a
workflow, connector, knowledge source or skill also runs through `subkit`:
the change is a file you can read and a command you can re-run.

Bare `subkit` opens an interactive prompt. Every command below also runs in
scripts and prints to stdout. `create --file`, `update --file`, `validate`,
`preview` and `probe` check a definition *before* it is saved. A mistake
then costs an error message, not a half-built connector someone has to
clean up.

The `requires` column names the permission that shows a command in
`--help`. The engine checks permissions again on every API call.

| command | requires | description | subcommands |
| ------- | -------- | ----------- | ----------- |
| `subkit agent` | `skill:read` | Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup | `briefing`, `capture`, `init` |
| `subkit apikeys` | `api_key:read` | Manage API keys | `create`, `list`, `revoke`, `rotate` |
| `subkit apps` | `settings:read` | The apps that sign their users in and call SubKit (products settings, sign-in providers, workflows, users, budget); erase-user removes one app user's SubKit data | `erase-user`, `list`, `show` |
| `subkit attach` | `file:write` | Upload a file and link it to a conversation (shortcut) | — |
| `subkit audit` | `audit:read` | Query the append-only audit log | `export`, `query`, `show` |
| `subkit auth` | `connector:write` | Start a connector's browser sign-in and print the URL to open. Works for every connector that signs in with an account — a web service or an MCP server; the engine names the route. | — |
| `subkit branding` | — | Read, update, reset, or download tenant branding | `get`, `logo`, `reset`, `update` |
| `subkit categories` | `workflow:read` | Show and rename the catalog categories shared by every kind | `list`, `rename` |
| `subkit chat` | `chat_workspace:read` | Manage external chat spaces (Google Chat / Slack) | `install-space`, `remove-space`, `spaces` |
| `subkit clipper` | — | Install the Chrome clipping extension | `install` |
| `subkit connector-templates` | `connector:read` | Manage connector templates | `create`, `delete`, `list`, `recipe`, `recipe-pack`, `recipes`, `search`, `set-oauth` |
| `subkit connectors` | `connector:read` | Manage connectors | `create`, `delete`, `disable`, `docs-delete`, `docs-ingest`, `docs-list`, `docs-search`, `enable`, `get`, `import`, `inspect`, `list`, `mcp-authorize`, `mcp-inspect`, `patch`, `probe`, `promote`, `test`, `validate` |
| `subkit diagnostics` | `audit:read` | Engine diagnostics: errors, LLM status, setup validation | `errors`, `llm`, `setup` |
| `subkit discovery` | `discovery:read` | Manage discovery runs and artifacts | `approve`, `artifacts`, `create`, `get`, `list`, `reject` |
| `subkit doctor` | — | Diagnose engine connectivity, authentication, and setup. Exits 0 (ok or warn) or 2 (blocked). | — |
| `subkit events` | `audit:read` | Query audit events | `get`, `list` |
| `subkit executions` | `execution:read` | Manage workflow executions | `abort`, `get`, `list`, `rerun`, `result`, `steps`, `tail` |
| `subkit extract` | `conversation:write` | Extract structured data from a file (LLM for text, native parsers for binary) | — |
| `subkit files` | `file:read` | Manage files (upload, download, link, …) | `delete`, `download`, `get`, `link`, `list`, `patch`, `replace`, `restore`, `stats`, `upload`, `versions` |
| `subkit health` | — | Runtime posture: liveness, token budget, failing runs, risk signals, schema drift, and process runtime. Use `subkit doctor` for connectivity/setup. | — |
| `subkit hooks` | `inbound_hook:read` | Manage inbound webhook bindings | `create`, `delete`, `get`, `list` |
| `subkit init` | — | Complete first-run engine bootstrap (consumes the token printed at engine boot) | — |
| `subkit install` | `connector:write` | Guided setup for enterprise integrations | `github`, `google-workspace`, `hubspot`, `jira`, `salesforce`, `slack` |
| `subkit intake` | `intake:read` | List collected items and start a selected Chat review | `default`, `discard`, `list`, `move`, `restore`, `review` |
| `subkit invites` | `identity:read` | Manage user-provisioning invites | `list`, `revoke` |
| `subkit join` | — | Redeem an invite to provision your personal API key (no login required) | — |
| `subkit knowledge-sources` | `knowledge:read` | Manage knowledge sources | `analyze`, `create`, `delete`, `get`, `history`, `import`, `list`, `patch`, `restore`, `search` |
| `subkit login` | — | Authenticate against a subkit engine | — |
| `subkit logout` | — | Drop the active profile | — |
| `subkit logs` | `audit:read` | Tail the engine's runtime log ring. --follow streams via SSE; --since accepts 5m / 2h / 1d / ISO-8601. | — |
| `subkit ls` | — | List cached conversation sessions for the active profile | — |
| `subkit mcp` | — | Run a stdio MCP server proxied to the engine | — |
| `subkit notifications` | `notification:read` | Manage notification channels, rules, deliveries, and the inbox | `channels`, `deliveries`, `inbox`, `rules` |
| `subkit packages` | `package:import` | Move this workspace to another engine: export a package archive, import one with a reviewed plan, list past imports | `export`, `import`, `installs` |
| `subkit patch-candidates` | `workflow:read` | Manage patch candidates | `approve`, `get`, `list`, `preview`, `reject` |
| `subkit portal-tokens` | `portal_token:read` | Manage portal tokens | `create`, `list`, `revoke` |
| `subkit profile` | — | Manage named profiles (environments) | `add`, `delete`, `list`, `show`, `use` |
| `subkit rbac` | `rbac:read` | Manage RBAC roles, permissions, grants, groups, and hooks | `can`, `grants`, `groups`, `permissions`, `request-hooks`, `roles`, `users`, `whatcan` |
| `subkit rename` | — | Assign or change a short alias for a session (used by `subkit -r <alias>`) | — |
| `subkit review` | `workflow:read` | Aggregated approval digest: pending patch candidates, proposed skill candidates, and recent failed executions. | — |
| `subkit rm` | — | Drop a session from the local cache (the server-side conversation row is preserved) | — |
| `subkit schedules` | `workflow:read` | Scheduled workflow runs | `create`, `delete`, `list`, `pause`, `resume`, `update` |
| `subkit self-healing` | `workflow:write` | Trigger and review proactive drift scans (admin) | `list`, `scan`, `show` |
| `subkit sessions` | — | Manage locally-cached conversation sessions | `ls`, `rename`, `rm`, `search`, `show` |
| `subkit settings` | `settings:read` | List, read, write, or interactively configure engine settings (secrets always masked) | `configure`, `get`, `list`, `set` |
| `subkit show` | — | Show cached metadata for a session by id or alias | — |
| `subkit skill-candidates` | `skill:read` | Manage skill candidates | `approve`, `get`, `list`, `reject` |
| `subkit skills` | `skill:read` | Manage skills | `activate`, `archive`, `create`, `delete`, `edit`, `get`, `history`, `list`, `patch`, `restore`, `sync` |
| `subkit stats` | `stats:read` | Tenant-scoped runtime statistics (needs stats:read) | `chat`, `connectors`, `conversations`, `events`, `executions`, `http`, `llm`, `mcp`, `operations` |
| `subkit status` | — | Print the active profile + engine reachability | — |
| `subkit subscriptions` | `subscription:read` | Manage event subscriptions | `create`, `delete`, `deliveries`, `get`, `list`, `patch`, `replay` |
| `subkit system` | `system:restart` | Engine process operations (restart) | `restart` |
| `subkit system-accounts` | `identity:read` | Manage system accounts | `create`, `delete`, `list` |
| `subkit tasks` | `task:read` | Tasks: a goal with limits that works on its own and asks before it acts | `abort`, `create`, `delete`, `get`, `list`, `pause`, `resume`, `run`, `runs`, `update` |
| `subkit tenants` | — | List tenants you belong to or switch the active one | — |
| `subkit update` | — | Update the subkit CLI to the latest release, or to the version of your engine | — |
| `subkit users` | `identity:read` | Manage identity users | `create`, `delete`, `get`, `invite`, `list`, `patch` |
| `subkit vault` | — | The vault (Tresor): secrets, logins and connector credentials. Workflows name an item as ${secret.<name>}; values never reach the model. | `add`, `attach`, `connector`, `list`, `refresh`, `reveal`, `rm`, `rotate`, `show` |
| `subkit workflows` | `workflow:read` | Manage workflows | `create`, `delete`, `dry-run`, `get`, `history`, `invoke-snippet`, `list`, `patch`, `preview`, `restore`, `run`, `update`, `validate` |

## Commands and arguments

Every argument of every command. `<name>` is positional; `--name` is a flag.

### `subkit agent`

Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup

#### `subkit agent briefing`

Print or verify the domain-scoped session briefing for coding agents

- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .subkit/agent.json of the repo; without hooks, else the known domains the repository name names)
- `--budget` (string) — Token budget for the briefing
- `--hook` (default: false) — Hook mode for Codex and Claude Code: inject a repository briefing and show a non-blocking status or warning
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit agent capture`

Send a session transcript to the engine to collect learnings for review

- `--transcript` (string) — Path to the transcript file (JSONL or text)
- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .subkit/agent.json of the repo)
- `--agent` (string, default: claude-code) — Producing agent name
- `--session-id` (string) — Session id for evidence attribution
- `--hook` (default: false) — SessionEnd/Stop-hook mode: read hook JSON from stdin, never fail
- `--detach` (default: false) — Process the hook payload in a detached process
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit agent init`

Set up automatic SubKit briefings for this repository in Claude Code and Codex

- `--domains` (string, required) — Comma-separated domains for this repository (e.g. accounting, blog-de)
- `--budget` (string) — Optional token budget for each briefing
- `--skip-claude` (default: false) — Do not touch ~/.claude/settings.json
- `--skip-codex` (default: false) — Do not touch ~/.codex/hooks.json


### `subkit apikeys`

Manage API keys

#### `subkit apikeys create`

Issue a new API key (shown once)

- `--name` (string) — Friendly key name (label)
- `--expires` (string) — Expiry — ISO-8601 timestamp
- `--scopes` (string) — Comma-separated scope strings (e.g. "workflow:read,workflow:run"). Defaults to your own credential's scopes; ["*"] (full role-derived access, and read-and-execute over MCP) only when your credential has no scope limits. Add "mcp:authoring" for a key that may also author definitions over MCP (a coding agent); leave it off for a key going into a browser client.
- `--allowed-workflows` (string) — Comma-separated workflow ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".
- `--allowed-connectors` (string) — Comma-separated connector ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".

#### `subkit apikeys list`

List API keys

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit apikeys revoke`

Revoke an API key

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Key id

#### `subkit apikeys rotate`

Rotate an API key (new key shown once)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Key id


### `subkit apps`

The apps that sign their users in and call SubKit (products settings, sign-in providers, workflows, users, budget); erase-user removes one app user's SubKit data

#### `subkit apps erase-user`

Erase an app user: removes SubKit's own data about that person for this app; the account at the sign-in provider stays. Irreversible

- `<app>` (positional, required) — App id (the product_id)
- `<user>` (positional, required) — User id (listed by subkit apps show <app>)
- `--yes` (default: false) — Confirm the erasure without asking
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit apps list`

List the apps of this workspace with environment, users, budget today and readiness

- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit apps show`

Show one app: settings, sign-in, workflows, users, today's budget and readiness with the next action

- `<id>` (positional, required) — App id (the product_id)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `subkit attach`

Upload a file and link it to a conversation (shortcut)

- `<conversation-id>` (positional, required) — Conversation id (UUID)
- `<path>` (positional, required) — Path to file
- `--content-type` (string) — Override detected MIME type
- `--slug` (string) — Optional slug for the link
- `--role` (string) — Optional role for the link
- `--quiet` (default: false) — Suppress progress output
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `subkit audit`

Query the append-only audit log

#### `subkit audit export`

Stream audit log as NDJSON to stdout or a file

- `--since` (string) — Lower bound — ISO-8601 timestamp
- `--to` (string) — Exclusive UTC upper bound (ISO-8601)
- `--action` (string) — Action name filter
- `--actor` (string) — Actor id filter
- `--actor-type` (string) — Actor kind
- `--api-key-id` (string) — Recorded API key id
- `--session-id` (string) — Recorded session id
- `--access-type` (string) — Verified access type
- `--oauth-client-id` (string) — Verified OAuth client id
- `--request-source` (string) — Legacy recorded source (not verified)
- `--origin-source` (string) — Verified initiating source
- `--execution-source` (string) — Immediate server execution step
- `--correlation-id` (string) — Trusted audit correlation id
- `--resource-type` (string) — Resource type
- `--resource-types` (string) — Comma-separated resource types
- `--resource-id` (string) — Resource id
- `--result` (string) — success, denied or error
- `--trace-id` (string) — Trace id
- `--execution-id` (string) — Recorded execution id
- `--conversation-id` (string) — Recorded conversation id
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Recorded workflow id
- `--output` (string) — Output file path (default: stdout)

#### `subkit audit query`

Filter the audit log

- `--limit` (string) — Max rows
- `--since` (string) — Lower bound — ISO-8601 timestamp or relative (e.g. 10m, 1h, 7d)
- `--action` (string) — Action name filter
- `--actor` (string) — Actor id filter
- `--actor-type` (string) — Actor kind
- `--api-key-id` (string) — Recorded API key id
- `--session-id` (string) — Recorded session id
- `--access-type` (string) — Verified access type
- `--oauth-client-id` (string) — Verified OAuth client id
- `--request-source` (string) — Legacy recorded source (not verified)
- `--origin-source` (string) — Verified initiating source
- `--execution-source` (string) — Immediate server execution step
- `--correlation-id` (string) — Trusted audit correlation id
- `--resource-type` (string) — Resource type
- `--resource-types` (string) — Comma-separated resource types
- `--resource-id` (string) — Filter by resource id
- `--result` (string) — success, denied or error
- `--trace-id` (string) — Trace id
- `--execution-id` (string) — Recorded execution id
- `--conversation-id` (string) — Recorded conversation id
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Recorded workflow id
- `--to` (string) — Exclusive UTC upper bound (ISO-8601)
- `--cursor` (string) — Continue after a previous page (its next_cursor)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit audit show`

Fetch one audit event by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Audit event id


### `subkit auth`

Start a connector's browser sign-in and print the URL to open. Works for every connector that signs in with an account — a web service or an MCP server; the engine names the route.

- `--connector-id` (string, required) — Connector to reauthenticate
- `--json` — Emit the full response as JSON


### `subkit branding`

Read, update, reset, or download tenant branding

#### `subkit branding get`

Read tenant branding

- `--engine-url` (string)
- `--api-key` (string)
- `--profile` (string)
- `--json`

#### `subkit branding logo`

Download normalized branding logo PNG

- `<theme>` (positional, required) — light or dark
- `--output` (string) — Output file, defaults to stdout
- `--revision` (string)
- `--engine-url` (string)
- `--api-key` (string)
- `--profile` (string)
- `--json`

#### `subkit branding reset`

Reset branding at an expected revision

- `<revision>` (positional, required)
- `--engine-url` (string)
- `--api-key` (string)
- `--profile` (string)
- `--json`

#### `subkit branding update`

Replace branding from canonical JSON body (file or - for stdin)

- `<input>` (positional, required) — JSON file or -
- `--engine-url` (string)
- `--api-key` (string)
- `--profile` (string)
- `--json`


### `subkit categories`

Show and rename the catalog categories shared by every kind

#### `subkit categories list`

List the catalog categories with how many workflows, connectors, knowledge sources, skills, files and tasks use each

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit categories rename`

Rename across all kinds with revision checks; preserve purpose ownership and merge into an existing target

- `<from>` (positional, required) — Current category
- `<to>` (positional, required) — New category
- `--json` — JSON output


### `subkit chat`

Manage external chat spaces (Google Chat / Slack)

#### `subkit chat install-space`

Register a chat space with the engine (Google Chat / Slack)

- `<platform>` (positional) — google_chat | slack
- `<workspace_id>` (positional) — Native space id, e.g. spaces/<id> (Slack: team id T…)
- `--bot-token` (string) — Slack bot token (xoxb-…) — required for slack
- `--default-channel` (string) — Optional default channel
- `--as` (string) — Installer platform user id (auto-filled from a pending space when omitted)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit chat remove-space`

Remove a chat-space install

- `<id>` (positional) — Chat workspace row id
- `--yes` — Skip confirmation
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit chat spaces`

List chat spaces installed in this tenant

- `--json` — JSON output


### `subkit clipper`

Install the Chrome clipping extension

#### `subkit clipper install`

Install the local Chrome clipping extension

- `--dir` (string) — Installation directory
- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine address (default: active profile)
- `--open` (default: true) — Open Chrome extensions after installing


### `subkit connector-templates`

Manage connector templates

#### `subkit connector-templates create`

Create a connector template

- `--role` (string) — Role: admin|member|enduser (default member)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit users delete`

Delete a user

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id

#### `subkit users get`

Fetch a user by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id

#### `subkit users invite`

Issue a single-use provisioning invite for a user (token shown once)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id to invite
- `--scopes` (string) — Comma-separated scope strings (default: your own credential's scopes; ["*"] only when your credential has no scope limits)
- `--allowed-workflows` (string) — Comma-separated workflow ids/slugs
- `--allowed-connectors` (string) — Comma-separated connector ids/slugs
- `--ttl` (string) — Invite lifetime in minutes
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit users list`

List identity users

- `--limit` (string) — Max rows
- `--app` (string) — Only users who signed in to this app (product_id, see subkit apps list)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit users patch`

Update a user's role (admin only)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id
- `--role` (string, required) — New role: admin|member|enduser


### `subkit vault`

The vault (Tresor): secrets, logins and connector credentials. Workflows name an item as ${secret.<name>}; values never reach the model.

#### `subkit vault add`

Add a secret or a login. The token or password is read from stdin or a hidden prompt, never from arguments.

- `<name>` (positional, required) — Handle name, e.g. crm-token
- `--kind` (string, default: secret) — secret | login
- `--username` (string) — login: the username
- `--scope` (string, default: workspace) — workspace | person
- `--env` (string, default: prod) — dev | prod
- `--description` (string) — What the item is for
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit vault attach`

Attach a connector's credential as a vault item. The secret comes from stdin or a hidden prompt, never from arguments: the token, the header or query value, the password, the PEM key, or for aws_sigv4 the secret access key and an optional session token on a second line.

- `<connector-id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--mode` (string, required) — bearer | header | query | basic | aws_sigv4 | signed_jwt | none
- `--header` (string) — header mode: the header name; without it stdin holds Name=Value lines
- `--query` (string) — query mode: the parameter name; without it stdin holds name=value lines
- `--username` (string) — basic mode username
- `--access-key-id` (string) — aws_sigv4 access key id
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the post-set connectivity probe
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `subkit vault connector`

List the vault items of one connector

- `<connector-id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit vault list`

List vault items: names and metadata, never values

- `--scope` (string) — workspace | person
- `--kind` (string) — connector | secret | login | template_client
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit vault refresh`

Refresh the OAuth token of a connector's vault item

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id

#### `subkit vault reveal`

Print a vault item's value. Every reveal is recorded in the audit log.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id
- `--field` (string) — Print only this field
- `--yes` — Confirm that the value may appear in this terminal

#### `subkit vault rm`

Delete a vault item and its value

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id

#### `subkit vault rotate`

Replace the value of a secret or login. The new value is read from stdin.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id
- `--username` (string) — login: a new username

#### `subkit vault show`

Show one vault item's metadata and activity

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id
- `--json` — JSON output


### `subkit workflows`

Manage workflows

#### `subkit workflows create`

Create a workflow from a JSON file (--file) or a solution recipe (--from-recipe <slug>, see `subkit connector-templates recipe-pack solutions`). Runs `validate` and `preview` by default; pass --skip-checks to bypass.

- `--file` (string) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--from-recipe` (string) — Slug of a solution recipe; its connectors are bound to the ones you already have
- `--bind` (string) — With --from-recipe: bind connectors yourself, as <template or placeholder>=<connector id or slug>[,…]; needed for templates without a fixed address such as http
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the pre-flight preview runs: dev (default) or prod. Use the environment the workflow's schedule or webhook runs in; writes stay held either way.
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the validate+preview pre-flight entirely (NOT recommended). Preview warnings never block; only validation errors and preview failures do.
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string passed to the preview dry-run. With --from-recipe it defaults to the recipe's sample input.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `subkit workflows delete`

Delete a workflow

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id

#### `subkit workflows dry-run`

Preview a draft WorkflowDef by dry-running it via runExecution (source=draft). No persistence. Alias: dry-run.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string
- `--name` (string) — Optional label (goes to executions.source_ref)
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the run executes: dev (default) or prod. Sent as the x-subkit-environment header; write steps need a connector bound to this environment.

#### `subkit workflows get`

Get a workflow by id

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id

#### `subkit workflows history`

List committed versions of a workflow

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit workflows invoke-snippet`

Emit a ready-to-paste, authenticated snippet to run a saved workflow from your own app or CI (curl/node/python).

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--lang` (string, default: curl) — Snippet language: curl (default), node, or python
- `--environment` (string, default: prod) — Where the call runs: prod (default) or dev. Printed as the x-subkit-environment header.
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit workflows list`

List workflows, grouped into catalog blocks

- `--limit` (string, default: 50) — Max rows
- `--category` (string) — Only this catalog block
- `--connector` (string) — Only workflows using this connector (id or slug)
- `--flat` — One flat table instead of grouped blocks
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit workflows patch`

Change a workflow's name, description or category without saving a new version (the slug and its wf_<slug> tool stay as they are).

- `<workflow>` (positional, required) — Workflow id or slug
- `--name` (string) — New display name
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `subkit categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `subkit workflows preview`

Preview a draft WorkflowDef by dry-running it via runExecution (source=draft). No persistence. Alias: dry-run.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string
- `--name` (string) — Optional label (goes to executions.source_ref)
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the run executes: dev (default) or prod. Sent as the x-subkit-environment header; write steps need a connector bound to this environment.

#### `subkit workflows restore`

Restore a prior workflow version

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `<version>` (positional, required) — Version number

#### `subkit workflows run`

Run a saved workflow, an inline draft definition, or a single step

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id or slug (omit when using --draft or --step)
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string. Prefix with `@` to read from a file (e.g. `--input @./payload.json`).
- `--input-file` (string) — Upload a file and substitute its ref into --input at key K. Format: K=<path>. Repeatable.
- `--draft` (string) — Path to a draft WorkflowDef JSON file (no commit)
- `--step` (string) — Path to a single StepDef JSON file (no workflow persistence)
- `--name` (string) — Optional label for --draft runs (goes to executions.source_ref)
- `--slug` (string) — Optional workflow_slug for --step runs (cosmetic)
- `--follow` — Queue the run and stream its progress live (step-by-step JSON lines). Saved workflows only.
- `--idempotency-key` (string) — Make this trigger safe to repeat: a second run with the same key is not started, the first run's id comes back instead. Saved workflows only.
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the run executes: dev (default) or prod. Sent as the x-subkit-environment header; write steps need a connector bound to this environment.

#### `subkit workflows update`

Update a workflow from a JSON file (PUT the full definition). Runs `validate` and `preview` by default; pass --skip-checks to bypass. An unchanged definition does not rotate a version.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--file` (string, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the pre-flight preview runs: dev (default) or prod. Use the environment the workflow's schedule or webhook runs in; writes stay held either way.
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the validate+preview pre-flight entirely (NOT recommended). Preview warnings never block; only validation errors and preview failures do.
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string passed to the preview dry-run.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `subkit workflows validate`

Validate a draft WorkflowDef JSON file (structural + step schema checks). No execution, no persistence.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON

de.title: subkit-CLI-Referenz
de.summary: Schlag jeden subkit-Befehl mit seinen Argumenten nach.
de.body:
Hier steht jeder Befehl der Kommandozeile `subkit` mit allen Argumenten. Die Kommandozeile bekommst du direkt von deiner Engine. Mit ihr entwirfst, änderst und startest du Workflows, Connectors, Quellen und Skills als Dateien. Jede Änderung ist eine Datei, die du lesen kannst, und ein Befehl, den du wiederholen kannst.

Die Referenz unten wird aus der CLI erzeugt und ist deshalb auf Englisch.

# subkit CLI reference

Look up every `subkit` command and argument here. Creating or changing a
workflow, connector, knowledge source or skill also runs through `subkit`:
the change is a file you can read and a command you can re-run.

Bare `subkit` opens an interactive prompt. Every command below also runs in
scripts and prints to stdout. `create --file`, `update --file`, `validate`,
`preview` and `probe` check a definition *before* it is saved. A mistake
then costs an error message, not a half-built connector someone has to
clean up.

The `requires` column names the permission that shows a command in
`--help`. The engine checks permissions again on every API call.

| command | requires | description | subcommands |
| ------- | -------- | ----------- | ----------- |
| `subkit agent` | `skill:read` | Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup | `briefing`, `capture`, `init` |
| `subkit apikeys` | `api_key:read` | Manage API keys | `create`, `list`, `revoke`, `rotate` |
| `subkit apps` | `settings:read` | The apps that sign their users in and call SubKit (products settings, sign-in providers, workflows, users, budget); erase-user removes one app user's SubKit data | `erase-user`, `list`, `show` |
| `subkit attach` | `file:write` | Upload a file and link it to a conversation (shortcut) | — |
| `subkit audit` | `audit:read` | Query the append-only audit log | `export`, `query`, `show` |
| `subkit auth` | `connector:write` | Start a connector's browser sign-in and print the URL to open. Works for every connector that signs in with an account — a web service or an MCP server; the engine names the route. | — |
| `subkit branding` | — | Read, update, reset, or download tenant branding | `get`, `logo`, `reset`, `update` |
| `subkit categories` | `workflow:read` | Show and rename the catalog categories shared by every kind | `list`, `rename` |
| `subkit chat` | `chat_workspace:read` | Manage external chat spaces (Google Chat / Slack) | `install-space`, `remove-space`, `spaces` |
| `subkit clipper` | — | Install the Chrome clipping extension | `install` |
| `subkit connector-templates` | `connector:read` | Manage connector templates | `create`, `delete`, `list`, `recipe`, `recipe-pack`, `recipes`, `search`, `set-oauth` |
| `subkit connectors` | `connector:read` | Manage connectors | `create`, `delete`, `disable`, `docs-delete`, `docs-ingest`, `docs-list`, `docs-search`, `enable`, `get`, `import`, `inspect`, `list`, `mcp-authorize`, `mcp-inspect`, `patch`, `probe`, `promote`, `test`, `validate` |
| `subkit diagnostics` | `audit:read` | Engine diagnostics: errors, LLM status, setup validation | `errors`, `llm`, `setup` |
| `subkit discovery` | `discovery:read` | Manage discovery runs and artifacts | `approve`, `artifacts`, `create`, `get`, `list`, `reject` |
| `subkit doctor` | — | Diagnose engine connectivity, authentication, and setup. Exits 0 (ok or warn) or 2 (blocked). | — |
| `subkit events` | `audit:read` | Query audit events | `get`, `list` |
| `subkit executions` | `execution:read` | Manage workflow executions | `abort`, `get`, `list`, `rerun`, `result`, `steps`, `tail` |
| `subkit extract` | `conversation:write` | Extract structured data from a file (LLM for text, native parsers for binary) | — |
| `subkit files` | `file:read` | Manage files (upload, download, link, …) | `delete`, `download`, `get`, `link`, `list`, `patch`, `replace`, `restore`, `stats`, `upload`, `versions` |
| `subkit health` | — | Runtime posture: liveness, token budget, failing runs, risk signals, schema drift, and process runtime. Use `subkit doctor` for connectivity/setup. | — |
| `subkit hooks` | `inbound_hook:read` | Manage inbound webhook bindings | `create`, `delete`, `get`, `list` |
| `subkit init` | — | Complete first-run engine bootstrap (consumes the token printed at engine boot) | — |
| `subkit install` | `connector:write` | Guided setup for enterprise integrations | `github`, `google-workspace`, `hubspot`, `jira`, `salesforce`, `slack` |
| `subkit intake` | `intake:read` | List collected items and start a selected Chat review | `default`, `discard`, `list`, `move`, `restore`, `review` |
| `subkit invites` | `identity:read` | Manage user-provisioning invites | `list`, `revoke` |
| `subkit join` | — | Redeem an invite to provision your personal API key (no login required) | — |
| `subkit knowledge-sources` | `knowledge:read` | Manage knowledge sources | `analyze`, `create`, `delete`, `get`, `history`, `import`, `list`, `patch`, `restore`, `search` |
| `subkit login` | — | Authenticate against a subkit engine | — |
| `subkit logout` | — | Drop the active profile | — |
| `subkit logs` | `audit:read` | Tail the engine's runtime log ring. --follow streams via SSE; --since accepts 5m / 2h / 1d / ISO-8601. | — |
| `subkit ls` | — | List cached conversation sessions for the active profile | — |
| `subkit mcp` | — | Run a stdio MCP server proxied to the engine | — |
| `subkit notifications` | `notification:read` | Manage notification channels, rules, deliveries, and the inbox | `channels`, `deliveries`, `inbox`, `rules` |
| `subkit packages` | `package:import` | Move this workspace to another engine: export a package archive, import one with a reviewed plan, list past imports | `export`, `import`, `installs` |
| `subkit patch-candidates` | `workflow:read` | Manage patch candidates | `approve`, `get`, `list`, `preview`, `reject` |
| `subkit portal-tokens` | `portal_token:read` | Manage portal tokens | `create`, `list`, `revoke` |
| `subkit profile` | — | Manage named profiles (environments) | `add`, `delete`, `list`, `show`, `use` |
| `subkit rbac` | `rbac:read` | Manage RBAC roles, permissions, grants, groups, and hooks | `can`, `grants`, `groups`, `permissions`, `request-hooks`, `roles`, `users`, `whatcan` |
| `subkit rename` | — | Assign or change a short alias for a session (used by `subkit -r <alias>`) | — |
| `subkit review` | `workflow:read` | Aggregated approval digest: pending patch candidates, proposed skill candidates, and recent failed executions. | — |
| `subkit rm` | — | Drop a session from the local cache (the server-side conversation row is preserved) | — |
| `subkit schedules` | `workflow:read` | Scheduled workflow runs | `create`, `delete`, `list`, `pause`, `resume`, `update` |
| `subkit self-healing` | `workflow:write` | Trigger and review proactive drift scans (admin) | `list`, `scan`, `show` |
| `subkit sessions` | — | Manage locally-cached conversation sessions | `ls`, `rename`, `rm`, `search`, `show` |
| `subkit settings` | `settings:read` | List, read, write, or interactively configure engine settings (secrets always masked) | `configure`, `get`, `list`, `set` |
| `subkit show` | — | Show cached metadata for a session by id or alias | — |
| `subkit skill-candidates` | `skill:read` | Manage skill candidates | `approve`, `get`, `list`, `reject` |
| `subkit skills` | `skill:read` | Manage skills | `activate`, `archive`, `create`, `delete`, `edit`, `get`, `history`, `list`, `patch`, `restore`, `sync` |
| `subkit stats` | `stats:read` | Tenant-scoped runtime statistics (needs stats:read) | `chat`, `connectors`, `conversations`, `events`, `executions`, `http`, `llm`, `mcp`, `operations` |
| `subkit status` | — | Print the active profile + engine reachability | — |
| `subkit subscriptions` | `subscription:read` | Manage event subscriptions | `create`, `delete`, `deliveries`, `get`, `list`, `patch`, `replay` |
| `subkit system` | `system:restart` | Engine process operations (restart) | `restart` |
| `subkit system-accounts` | `identity:read` | Manage system accounts | `create`, `delete`, `list` |
| `subkit tasks` | `task:read` | Tasks: a goal with limits that works on its own and asks before it acts | `abort`, `create`, `delete`, `get`, `list`, `pause`, `resume`, `run`, `runs`, `update` |
| `subkit tenants` | — | List tenants you belong to or switch the active one | — |
| `subkit update` | — | Update the subkit CLI to the latest release, or to the version of your engine | — |
| `subkit users` | `identity:read` | Manage identity users | `create`, `delete`, `get`, `invite`, `list`, `patch` |
| `subkit vault` | — | The vault (Tresor): secrets, logins and connector credentials. Workflows name an item as ${secret.<name>}; values never reach the model. | `add`, `attach`, `connector`, `list`, `refresh`, `reveal`, `rm`, `rotate`, `show` |
| `subkit workflows` | `workflow:read` | Manage workflows | `create`, `delete`, `dry-run`, `get`, `history`, `invoke-snippet`, `list`, `patch`, `preview`, `restore`, `run`, `update`, `validate` |

## Commands and arguments

Every argument of every command. `<name>` is positional; `--name` is a flag.

### `subkit agent`

Coding-agent integration: session briefings and hook setup

#### `subkit agent briefing`

Print or verify the domain-scoped session briefing for coding agents

- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .subkit/agent.json of the repo; without hooks, else the known domains the repository name names)
- `--budget` (string) — Token budget for the briefing
- `--hook` (default: false) — Hook mode for Codex and Claude Code: inject a repository briefing and show a non-blocking status or warning
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit agent capture`

Send a session transcript to the engine to collect learnings for review

- `--transcript` (string) — Path to the transcript file (JSONL or text)
- `--domains` (string) — Comma-separated domain slugs (default: .subkit/agent.json of the repo)
- `--agent` (string, default: claude-code) — Producing agent name
- `--session-id` (string) — Session id for evidence attribution
- `--hook` (default: false) — SessionEnd/Stop-hook mode: read hook JSON from stdin, never fail
- `--detach` (default: false) — Process the hook payload in a detached process
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit agent init`

Set up automatic SubKit briefings for this repository in Claude Code and Codex

- `--domains` (string, required) — Comma-separated domains for this repository (e.g. accounting, blog-de)
- `--budget` (string) — Optional token budget for each briefing
- `--skip-claude` (default: false) — Do not touch ~/.claude/settings.json
- `--skip-codex` (default: false) — Do not touch ~/.codex/hooks.json


### `subkit apikeys`

Manage API keys

#### `subkit apikeys create`

Issue a new API key (shown once)

- `--name` (string) — Friendly key name (label)
- `--expires` (string) — Expiry — ISO-8601 timestamp
- `--scopes` (string) — Comma-separated scope strings (e.g. "workflow:read,workflow:run"). Defaults to your own credential's scopes; ["*"] (full role-derived access, and read-and-execute over MCP) only when your credential has no scope limits. Add "mcp:authoring" for a key that may also author definitions over MCP (a coding agent); leave it off for a key going into a browser client.
- `--allowed-workflows` (string) — Comma-separated workflow ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".
- `--allowed-connectors` (string) — Comma-separated connector ids/slugs. Use "*" for explicit "all".

#### `subkit apikeys list`

List API keys

- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit apikeys revoke`

Revoke an API key

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Key id

#### `subkit apikeys rotate`

Rotate an API key (new key shown once)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Key id


### `subkit apps`

The apps that sign their users in and call SubKit (products settings, sign-in providers, workflows, users, budget); erase-user removes one app user's SubKit data

#### `subkit apps erase-user`

Erase an app user: removes SubKit's own data about that person for this app; the account at the sign-in provider stays. Irreversible

- `<app>` (positional, required) — App id (the product_id)
- `<user>` (positional, required) — User id (listed by subkit apps show <app>)
- `--yes` (default: false) — Confirm the erasure without asking
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit apps list`

List the apps of this workspace with environment, users, budget today and readiness

- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit apps show`

Show one app: settings, sign-in, workflows, users, today's budget and readiness with the next action

- `<id>` (positional, required) — App id (the product_id)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `subkit attach`

Upload a file and link it to a conversation (shortcut)

- `<conversation-id>` (positional, required) — Conversation id (UUID)
- `<path>` (positional, required) — Path to file
- `--content-type` (string) — Override detected MIME type
- `--slug` (string) — Optional slug for the link
- `--role` (string) — Optional role for the link
- `--quiet` (default: false) — Suppress progress output
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `subkit audit`

Query the append-only audit log

#### `subkit audit export`

Stream audit log as NDJSON to stdout or a file

- `--since` (string) — Lower bound — ISO-8601 timestamp
- `--to` (string) — Exclusive UTC upper bound (ISO-8601)
- `--action` (string) — Action name filter
- `--actor` (string) — Actor id filter
- `--actor-type` (string) — Actor kind
- `--api-key-id` (string) — Recorded API key id
- `--session-id` (string) — Recorded session id
- `--access-type` (string) — Verified access type
- `--oauth-client-id` (string) — Verified OAuth client id
- `--request-source` (string) — Legacy recorded source (not verified)
- `--origin-source` (string) — Verified initiating source
- `--execution-source` (string) — Immediate server execution step
- `--correlation-id` (string) — Trusted audit correlation id
- `--resource-type` (string) — Resource type
- `--resource-types` (string) — Comma-separated resource types
- `--resource-id` (string) — Resource id
- `--result` (string) — success, denied or error
- `--trace-id` (string) — Trace id
- `--execution-id` (string) — Recorded execution id
- `--conversation-id` (string) — Recorded conversation id
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Recorded workflow id
- `--output` (string) — Output file path (default: stdout)

#### `subkit audit query`

Filter the audit log

- `--limit` (string) — Max rows
- `--since` (string) — Lower bound — ISO-8601 timestamp or relative (e.g. 10m, 1h, 7d)
- `--action` (string) — Action name filter
- `--actor` (string) — Actor id filter
- `--actor-type` (string) — Actor kind
- `--api-key-id` (string) — Recorded API key id
- `--session-id` (string) — Recorded session id
- `--access-type` (string) — Verified access type
- `--oauth-client-id` (string) — Verified OAuth client id
- `--request-source` (string) — Legacy recorded source (not verified)
- `--origin-source` (string) — Verified initiating source
- `--execution-source` (string) — Immediate server execution step
- `--correlation-id` (string) — Trusted audit correlation id
- `--resource-type` (string) — Resource type
- `--resource-types` (string) — Comma-separated resource types
- `--resource-id` (string) — Filter by resource id
- `--result` (string) — success, denied or error
- `--trace-id` (string) — Trace id
- `--execution-id` (string) — Recorded execution id
- `--conversation-id` (string) — Recorded conversation id
- `--workflow-id` (string) — Recorded workflow id
- `--to` (string) — Exclusive UTC upper bound (ISO-8601)
- `--cursor` (string) — Continue after a previous page (its next_cursor)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit audit show`

Fetch one audit event by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Audit event id


### `subkit auth`

- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks get`

Show a task, its latest run and whether its standing permission is live

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Task id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks list`

List tasks (your own; an admin sees all)

- `--category` (string) — Only this catalog block
- `--archived` (default: false) — Show archived tasks instead
- `--limit` (string, default: 50) — Max rows
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks pause`

Pause a task: no run starts and an open run sleeps until you resume it

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Task id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks resume`

Resume a paused task; a run that slept through the pause continues

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Task id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks run`

Start a task now, as you; the run works in its own conversation

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Task id
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks runs`

List the runs of a task, newest first

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Task id
- `--limit` (string, default: 20) — Max rows
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output

#### `subkit tasks update`

Replace a task from a JSON file (--file) or change only its schedule (--cron with --timezone, or --run-at); a content change stops the open run and ends the standing permission

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Task id
- `--file` (string) — Path to the task JSON file
- `--cron` (string) — New 5-field cron (e.g. "0 8 * * 1-5")
- `--timezone` (string) — New IANA timezone (default UTC)
- `--run-at` (string) — Run once at this ISO instant (e.g. 2026-12-01T07:00:00+01:00)
- `--json` (default: false) — JSON output


### `subkit tenants`

List tenants you belong to or switch the active one

- `--engine-url` (string) — Engine base URL
- `--api-key` (string) — API key (Bearer)
- `--tenant` (string) — Active tenant id
- `--profile` (string) — Profile name (~/.subkit/config.json)
- `--verbose` — Print each request with its trace id and timing to stderr (same as SUBKIT_DEBUG=1)
- `<use>` (positional) — Tenant id to switch to


### `subkit update`

Update the subkit CLI to the latest release, or to the version of your engine

- `--check` (default: false) — Report whether an update exists without installing it
- `--force` (default: false) — Download and install even when already up to date
- `--match-engine` (default: false) — Install the version the engine of the active profile runs
- `--rollback` (default: false) — Restore the most recently retained subkit binary
- `--to` (string) — With --rollback, the retained version to restore (default: the most recent)


### `subkit users`

Manage identity users

#### `subkit users create`

Create a user in the caller's tenant

- `--email` (string, required) — User email
- `--role` (string) — Role: admin|member|enduser (default member)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit users delete`

Delete a user

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id

#### `subkit users get`

Fetch a user by id

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id

#### `subkit users invite`

Issue a single-use provisioning invite for a user (token shown once)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id to invite
- `--scopes` (string) — Comma-separated scope strings (default: your own credential's scopes; ["*"] only when your credential has no scope limits)
- `--allowed-workflows` (string) — Comma-separated workflow ids/slugs
- `--allowed-connectors` (string) — Comma-separated connector ids/slugs
- `--ttl` (string) — Invite lifetime in minutes
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit users list`

List identity users

- `--limit` (string) — Max rows
- `--app` (string) — Only users who signed in to this app (product_id, see subkit apps list)
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit users patch`

Update a user's role (admin only)

- `<id>` (positional, required) — User id
- `--role` (string, required) — New role: admin|member|enduser


### `subkit vault`

The vault (Tresor): secrets, logins and connector credentials. Workflows name an item as ${secret.<name>}; values never reach the model.

#### `subkit vault add`

Add a secret or a login. The token or password is read from stdin or a hidden prompt, never from arguments.

- `<name>` (positional, required) — Handle name, e.g. crm-token
- `--kind` (string, default: secret) — secret | login
- `--username` (string) — login: the username
- `--scope` (string, default: workspace) — workspace | person
- `--env` (string, default: prod) — dev | prod
- `--description` (string) — What the item is for
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit vault attach`

Attach a connector's credential as a vault item. The secret comes from stdin or a hidden prompt, never from arguments: the token, the header or query value, the password, the PEM key, or for aws_sigv4 the secret access key and an optional session token on a second line.

- `<connector-id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--mode` (string, required) — bearer | header | query | basic | aws_sigv4 | signed_jwt | none
- `--header` (string) — header mode: the header name; without it stdin holds Name=Value lines
- `--query` (string) — query mode: the parameter name; without it stdin holds name=value lines
- `--username` (string) — basic mode username
- `--access-key-id` (string) — aws_sigv4 access key id
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the post-set connectivity probe
- `--json` — JSON-only output

#### `subkit vault connector`

List the vault items of one connector

- `<connector-id>` (positional, required) — Connector id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit vault list`

List vault items: names and metadata, never values

- `--scope` (string) — workspace | person
- `--kind` (string) — connector | secret | login | template_client
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit vault refresh`

Refresh the OAuth token of a connector's vault item

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id

#### `subkit vault reveal`

Print a vault item's value. Every reveal is recorded in the audit log.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id
- `--field` (string) — Print only this field
- `--yes` — Confirm that the value may appear in this terminal

#### `subkit vault rm`

Delete a vault item and its value

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id

#### `subkit vault rotate`

Replace the value of a secret or login. The new value is read from stdin.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id
- `--username` (string) — login: a new username

#### `subkit vault show`

Show one vault item's metadata and activity

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Vault item id
- `--json` — JSON output


### `subkit workflows`

Manage workflows

#### `subkit workflows create`

Create a workflow from a JSON file (--file) or a solution recipe (--from-recipe <slug>, see `subkit connector-templates recipe-pack solutions`). Runs `validate` and `preview` by default; pass --skip-checks to bypass.

- `--file` (string) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--from-recipe` (string) — Slug of a solution recipe; its connectors are bound to the ones you already have
- `--bind` (string) — With --from-recipe: bind connectors yourself, as <template or placeholder>=<connector id or slug>[,…]; needed for templates without a fixed address such as http
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the pre-flight preview runs: dev (default) or prod. Use the environment the workflow's schedule or webhook runs in; writes stay held either way.
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the validate+preview pre-flight entirely (NOT recommended). Preview warnings never block; only validation errors and preview failures do.
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string passed to the preview dry-run. With --from-recipe it defaults to the recipe's sample input.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `subkit workflows delete`

Delete a workflow

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id

#### `subkit workflows dry-run`

Preview a draft WorkflowDef by dry-running it via runExecution (source=draft). No persistence. Alias: dry-run.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string
- `--name` (string) — Optional label (goes to executions.source_ref)
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the run executes: dev (default) or prod. Sent as the x-subkit-environment header; write steps need a connector bound to this environment.

#### `subkit workflows get`

Get a workflow by id

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id

#### `subkit workflows history`

List committed versions of a workflow

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit workflows invoke-snippet`

Emit a ready-to-paste, authenticated snippet to run a saved workflow from your own app or CI (curl/node/python).

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--lang` (string, default: curl) — Snippet language: curl (default), node, or python
- `--environment` (string, default: prod) — Where the call runs: prod (default) or dev. Printed as the x-subkit-environment header.
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit workflows list`

List workflows, grouped into catalog blocks

- `--limit` (string, default: 50) — Max rows
- `--category` (string) — Only this catalog block
- `--connector` (string) — Only workflows using this connector (id or slug)
- `--flat` — One flat table instead of grouped blocks
- `--json` — JSON output

#### `subkit workflows patch`

Change a workflow's name, description or category without saving a new version (the slug and its wf_<slug> tool stay as they are).

- `<workflow>` (positional, required) — Workflow id or slug
- `--name` (string) — New display name
- `--description` (string) — What it is for, in plain language — the assistant reads this to pick the right object. "" hands it back to automatic description.
- `--category` (string) — Catalog block, lowercase words joined by dashes (see `subkit categories list`). "" hands it back to automatic categorisation.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `subkit workflows preview`

Preview a draft WorkflowDef by dry-running it via runExecution (source=draft). No persistence. Alias: dry-run.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string
- `--name` (string) — Optional label (goes to executions.source_ref)
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the run executes: dev (default) or prod. Sent as the x-subkit-environment header; write steps need a connector bound to this environment.

#### `subkit workflows restore`

Restore a prior workflow version

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `<version>` (positional, required) — Version number

#### `subkit workflows run`

Run a saved workflow, an inline draft definition, or a single step

- `<id>` (positional) — Workflow id or slug (omit when using --draft or --step)
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string. Prefix with `@` to read from a file (e.g. `--input @./payload.json`).
- `--input-file` (string) — Upload a file and substitute its ref into --input at key K. Format: K=<path>. Repeatable.
- `--draft` (string) — Path to a draft WorkflowDef JSON file (no commit)
- `--step` (string) — Path to a single StepDef JSON file (no workflow persistence)
- `--name` (string) — Optional label for --draft runs (goes to executions.source_ref)
- `--slug` (string) — Optional workflow_slug for --step runs (cosmetic)
- `--follow` — Queue the run and stream its progress live (step-by-step JSON lines). Saved workflows only.
- `--idempotency-key` (string) — Make this trigger safe to repeat: a second run with the same key is not started, the first run's id comes back instead. Saved workflows only.
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the run executes: dev (default) or prod. Sent as the x-subkit-environment header; write steps need a connector bound to this environment.

#### `subkit workflows update`

Update a workflow from a JSON file (PUT the full definition). Runs `validate` and `preview` by default; pass --skip-checks to bypass. An unchanged definition does not rotate a version.

- `<id>` (positional, required) — Workflow id
- `--file` (string, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON
- `--environment` (string, default: dev) — Where the pre-flight preview runs: dev (default) or prod. Use the environment the workflow's schedule or webhook runs in; writes stay held either way.
- `--skip-checks` — Skip the validate+preview pre-flight entirely (NOT recommended). Preview warnings never block; only validation errors and preview failures do.
- `--input` (string) — Input JSON string passed to the preview dry-run.
- `--json` — JSON-only output (suppresses narration)

#### `subkit workflows validate`

Validate a draft WorkflowDef JSON file (structural + step schema checks). No execution, no persistence.

- `<file>` (positional, required) — Path to WorkflowDef JSON

en.title: SubKit runtime settings
en.summary: Look up every runtime setting with its description and default value.
en.body:
# SubKit runtime settings

Look up every runtime setting with its description and default value.
You change a value with `subkit settings configure` and `subkit settings set`, through the
HTTP or MCP settings APIs, or in the canonical config file. Per-tenant overrides go
into the file's `tenants` section and only apply to settings tagged `scope=tenant`.

A value resolves in this order: tenant overlay, then global value, then schema
default. Environment variables never set a runtime setting; only the bootstrap-only
process bindings `database.url`, `storage.backend`, `storage.filesystem.root` and
`deployment.mode` (from `SUBKIT_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`) come from the environment at startup.

## log
Logging

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `log.format` | enum("dev" \| "pretty" \| "prod" \| "ndjson" \| "json") | `"ndjson"` | global | no | no | Log output format |
| `log.level` | enum("trace" \| "debug" \| "info" \| "warn" \| "error" \| "fatal") | `"info"` | global | no | no | Log verbosity |

## deployment
Deployment

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `deployment.mode` | enum("server" \| "local_workspace") | `"server"` | global | no | yes | Bootstrap-only deployment mode: server, or local_workspace when SubKit Desktop runs the engine on this device (loopback only, local sign-in, laptop profile). Set SUBKIT_DEPLOYMENT_MODE and restart. |

## server
HTTP server

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `server.desktop_dev_callback` | boolean | `false` | global | no | no | Also accept subkit-dev://callback as a sign-in target, for development builds of SubKit Desktop. Outside NODE_ENV=production it is accepted without this setting. |
| `server.desktop_min_version` | string | `"0.1.0"` | global | no | no | Oldest SubKit Desktop version this engine accepts. Published as clients.desktop.min_version in /.well-known/service-descriptor.json; an older app asks for an update instead of signing in. |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.global_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request ceiling across hosted ingress per minute; zero denies hosted ingress |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.peer_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request ceiling per verified connection peer and minute; zero denies hosted ingress |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.principal_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request ceiling per authenticated principal and tenant per minute; zero denies hosted requests |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.tenant_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request ceiling per hosted tenant and minute; zero denies hosted requests |
| `server.hosted_rate_limit.tenant_per_month` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator request allowance per hosted tenant and UTC calendar month; zero denies hosted requests |
| `server.port` | number | `3000` | global | no | yes | HTTP port to bind (1..65535) |
| `server.public_base_url` | string | `""` | global | no | no | External-facing URL the engine resolves at. Used by /install, chat link replies, and OAuth2 redirect-URI synthesis. Required for any OAuth2 connector. |
| `server.restart_supervised` | boolean | `false` | global | no | no | A supervisor (systemd with Restart=on-failure, Docker with a restart policy) starts the engine again after it ends. Enables POST /v1/system/restart (exit code 75). |
| `server.root_redirect_to_cockpit` | boolean | `true` | global | no | no | Send a browser that opens / to the Cockpit at /cockpit. Agents keep the Markdown index. Set false to show browsers the engine index at /; it stays at /engine either way. |
| `server.trusted_proxy_hops` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Trusted reverse-proxy hops counted from the right of X-Forwarded-For; zero ignores forwarding headers. |
| `server.trusted_proxy_ips` | array | `[]` | global | no | no | Exact trusted reverse-proxy socket peer IPs. Every configured forwarding hop must match; X-Real-IP is never trusted. |

## database
Database connection

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `database.connect_timeout_ms` | number | `10000` | global | no | yes | Deadline for acquiring or establishing a PostgreSQL connection. |
| `database.idle_timeout_ms` | number | `30000` | global | no | yes | Time before an unused pooled connection is closed. |
| `database.keepalive_delay_ms` | number | `10000` | global | no | yes | Initial TCP keepalive delay for PostgreSQL connections. |
| `database.pool_max` | number | `10` | global | no | yes | Maximum application connections per pool and replica. |
| `database.query_timeout_ms` | number | `150000` | global | no | yes | Client-side PostgreSQL query deadline in milliseconds. |
| `database.statement_timeout_ms` | number | `120000` | global | no | yes | Server-side PostgreSQL statement deadline, initialized on each session. |
| `database.url` | string | `—` | global | yes | yes | Bootstrap-only Postgres connection string. Rotate DATABASE_URL and restart replicas; runtime revisions cannot change this binding. |

## llm
LLM configuration

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `llm.api_key` | string | `""` | tenant | yes | no | Primary LLM API key |
| `llm.context_1m` | boolean | `false` | tenant | no | no | Enable 1M context window where supported |
| `llm.critic.enabled` | boolean | `false` | tenant | no | no | Run the second-stage LLM critic on workflow drafts after every static gate passes |
| `llm.critic.max_consecutive_rejections` | number | `3` | tenant | no | no | After this many consecutive critic_rejected results in a conversation, skip the critic to avoid an infinite re-author loop |
| `llm.critic.min_steps` | number | `3` | tenant | no | no | Minimum step count for the critic to run on a draft (drift in recent drafts also triggers a run) |
| `llm.fallback_model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no | Fallback model identifier |
| `llm.fallback_provider` | enum("mock" \| "anthropic" \| "openai" \| "gemini" \| "azure" \| "bedrock" \| "vertex" \| "ai_gateway") | `null` | tenant | no | no | Fallback provider on primary failure |
| `llm.model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no | Primary model identifier |
| `llm.output_guard` | enum("soft" \| "hard" \| "off") | `"soft"` | global | no | no | LLM output safety mode (soft: rewrite + log, hard: throw, off: bypass — never use in production) |
| `llm.provider` | enum("mock" \| "anthropic" \| "openai" \| "gemini" \| "azure" \| "bedrock" \| "vertex" \| "ai_gateway") | `"mock"` | tenant | no | no | Primary LLM provider |
| `llm.providers.ai_gateway.api_key` | string | `""` | global | yes | no |  |
| `llm.providers.ai_gateway.model` | string | `""` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.anthropic.api_key` | string | `""` | tenant | yes | no | API key for this provider |
| `llm.providers.anthropic.base_url` | string | `""` | global | no | no | Optional base URL override |
| `llm.providers.anthropic.model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no | Default model identifier |
| `llm.providers.azure.api_key` | string | `""` | tenant | yes | no |  |
| `llm.providers.azure.api_version` | string | `""` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.azure.base_url` | string | `""` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.azure.model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.azure.resource_name` | string | `""` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.azure.use_deployment_based_urls` | boolean | `false` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.bedrock.access_key_id` | string | `""` | global | yes | no |  |
| `llm.providers.bedrock.base_url` | string | `""` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.bedrock.model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.bedrock.region` | string | `""` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.bedrock.secret_access_key` | string | `""` | global | yes | no |  |
| `llm.providers.bedrock.session_token` | string | `""` | global | yes | no |  |
| `llm.providers.gemini.api_key` | string | `""` | tenant | yes | no | API key for this provider |
| `llm.providers.gemini.base_url` | string | `""` | global | no | no | Optional base URL override |
| `llm.providers.gemini.model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no | Default model identifier |
| `llm.providers.openai.api_key` | string | `""` | tenant | yes | no | API key for this provider |
| `llm.providers.openai.base_url` | string | `""` | global | no | no | Optional base URL override |
| `llm.providers.openai.model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no | Default model identifier |
| `llm.providers.vertex.api_key` | string | `""` | tenant | yes | no |  |
| `llm.providers.vertex.client_email` | string | `""` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.vertex.google_application_credentials` | string | `""` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.vertex.location` | string | `""` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.vertex.model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no |  |
| `llm.providers.vertex.private_key` | string | `""` | global | yes | no |  |
| `llm.providers.vertex.project` | string | `""` | global | no | no |  |
| `llm.reasoning_effort` | enum("default" \| "none" \| "low" \| "medium" \| "high") | `"default"` | tenant | no | no | Reasoning effort in authoring turns. default: thinking only in late stages on supported Claude models. none, low, medium or high: every stage on OpenAI reasoning and supported Claude models. |
| `llm.suggestion_model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no | Small model used to generate post-turn suggestions; empty uses the primary provider's default |
| `llm.summarize_model` | string | `""` | tenant | no | no | Model used for summarization passes |
| `llm.summarize_provider` | enum("mock" \| "anthropic" \| "openai" \| "gemini" \| "azure" \| "bedrock" \| "vertex" \| "ai_gateway") | `null` | tenant | no | no | Provider used for summarization passes |
| `llm.web_search` | boolean | `true` | tenant | no | no | Allow the assistant to use Anthropic-native server-side web search (billed per search; Anthropic models only). Toggle off per tenant via /settings. |

## auth
Authentication

| path | type | default | scope | sensitive | requiresRestart | description |
| ---- | ---- | ------- | ----- | --------- | --------------- | ----------- |
| `auth.enable_signup` | boolean | `false` | global | no | no | Compatibility fallback for self-hosted OIDC providers without signup_policy: allow first-time SSO member accounts. Explicit provider policies override it; hosted signup never uses it. |
| `auth.hosted.admission.mcp_clients_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator global hosted MCP dynamic-client registration ceiling per minute. |
| `auth.hosted.admission.mcp_clients_per_peer_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator hosted MCP dynamic-client registration ceiling per verified peer and minute. |
| `auth.hosted.admission.retained_mcp_clients` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator ceiling for retained MCP client registrations, including retired and disabled clients; zero denies new clients. |
| `auth.hosted.admission.retained_tenants` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator ceiling for retained self-service tenant records, including erased ownership tombstones; zero denies new tenants. |
| `auth.hosted.admission.tenant_creations_per_minute` | number | `0` | global | no | no | Operator global ceiling for newly created self-service tenants per minute; idempotent callbacks do not consume it. |
| `auth.hosted.enabled` | boolean | `false` | global | no | yes | Enable identity-first hosted browser authentication for explicitly opted-in providers. |
| `auth.hosted.registration_enabled` | boolean | `false` | global | no | no | Allow new hosted identities to provision their own workspace. Existing members and reviewed invitation handoffs remain available while registration is closed. |
| `auth.mcp_oauth.access_token_ttl_seconds` | number | `3600` | global | no | no | Lifetime in seconds for MCP OAuth access tokens. |
| `auth.mcp_oauth.authorization_code_ttl_seconds` | number | `60` | global | no | no | Lifetime in seconds for MCP OAuth authorization codes. |
| `auth.mcp_oauth.dynamic_registration_enabled` | boolean | `true` | global | no | no | Allow RFC 7591 dynamic client registration at POST /v1/oauth/register. |
| `auth.mcp_oauth.enabled` | boolean | `true` | global | no | yes | Enable the MCP OAuth 2.1 authorization server (ChatGPT / Claude.ai / Cursor). |
| `auth.mcp_oauth.refresh_token_ttl_seconds` | number | `2592000` | global | no | no | Lifetime in seconds for MCP OAuth refresh tokens (30 days). |
| `auth.mcp_oauth.scopes_supported` | string[] | `["mcp:read","mcp:authoring","mcp:admin","metrics:read"]` | global | no | no | OAuth scopes advertised in the authorization server metadata. Add, reorder and remove freely, except metrics:read: GET /metrics enforces it, so it is restored whenever a written value omits it. |

## Workspace settings

Every workspace keeps its own name, time zone and language. They are not runtime settings: the workspace owner or a holder of `identity:write` changes them in the Cockpit under Settings › Workspace or with `PATCH /v1/identity/workspace`.

| field | type | default | description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `display_name` | string | `—` | Name of the workspace |
| `timezone` | string | `"UTC"` | IANA time zone, e.g. Europe/Berlin |
| `language` | enum("de" \| "en") | `"en"` | Language for texts that no person's language decides, such as device connector names and scheduled task runs; a person's own app language still wins |

Texts that no person's language decides follow the workspace language: device connector names when the desktop app sends no known language, and new tasks created without a language from the request. A person's own app language still wins; without either, the text is English.

## Authentication providers

`auth.providers` is one atomic, validated runtime setting available through Cockpit, HTTP, MCP, `subkit settings`, and the canonical config file. Records use `protocol: api_key` or `oidc`; one API-key adapter and multiple named direct OIDC adapters may coexist. Provider ids must be unique, and every OIDC callback is `/v1/identity/login/callback` on `server.public_base_url`. A successful write is active for subsequent browser-login requests without an engine restart.

OIDC records are public clients using Authorization Code with PKCE. Runtime configuration intentionally has no `client_secret` field and rejects one if supplied; use an issuer that supports public clients with `token_endpoint_auth_method=none`. The environment is not an auth-provider source.

Configured labels are diagnostic metadata only. The common `mcp-auth` surface derives its two user actions from protocol and always presents `Continue with SSO` before `Continue with API key`. Discovery exposes the canonical labels `SSO` and `API key`; no provider-specific route or parallel configuration tree is accepted.

## Filesystem object store

On a single device, the engine can keep files and offloaded results in a folder instead of an S3-compatible object store. Set two environment variables before the engine starts:

| Variable | Setting | Value |
| -------- | ------- | ----- |
| `OBJECT_STORAGE_BACKEND` | `storage.backend` | `filesystem` (default `s3`) |
| `OBJECT_STORAGE_ROOT` | `storage.filesystem.root` | absolute folder, for example `<app data>/local/<workspace>/files` |

Both are bootstrap-only: they come from the environment on every start, a stored revision cannot change them, and the settings APIs refuse to write them. The `storage.object_store` values are not needed in this mode.

- **Startup check:** the parent folder must exist. The engine creates the folder with mode `0700`, tightens an existing one to `0700`, and proves it can write, read, delete and hard-link inside it. If a check fails, the engine does not start and names the reason (`root_parent_missing`, `root_not_directory`, `root_not_writable`, `root_cross_device`, `root_no_hard_links`) with a remedy.
- **Writes:** each object is written to a staging file, flushed to disk, then linked into place, so a reader sees the whole object or nothing. An existing key is never overwritten. Files get mode `0600`, folders `0700`.
- **Keys:** every key segment is encoded to lowercase ASCII (`a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `-`, other bytes as `%xx`), so keys that differ only in case or Unicode form stay apart on case-insensitive disks, and Windows reserved names are safe. `..`, empty segments and absolute keys are refused, and a link that leads outside the folder is never followed.
- **Backup:** the folder is the whole object store; copy it together with the database dump.
- **Not supported:** network drives, cloud-synced folders and disks without hard links, such as exFAT.

de.title: Einstellungen
de.summary: Schlag jede Einstellung der Engine mit Beschreibung und Standardwert nach.

headings.text: Dateien in einem Ordner statt im Objektspeicher

de.body:
Hier steht jeder Wert der Laufzeitkonfiguration mit Beschreibung und Standardwert. Du änderst ihn mit `subkit settings configure` und `subkit settings set`, über die HTTP- oder MCP-Schnittstelle für Einstellungen oder in der Konfigurationsdatei `subkit.config.json`. Eigene Werte für einen Arbeitsbereich gelten nur bei Einstellungen, die dafür markiert sind (`scope=tenant`). Umgebungsvariablen setzen keine dieser Einstellungen. Ausnahmen sind die Bootstrap-Werte `database.url`, `storage.backend`, `storage.filesystem.root` und `deployment.mode` (aus `SUBKIT_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`) – diese Werte kommen bei jedem Start aus der Umgebung.

## Dateien in einem Ordner statt im Objektspeicher

Auf einem einzelnen Gerät legt die Engine Dateien und ausgelagerte Ergebnisse in einem Ordner ab statt in einem S3-kompatiblen Objektspeicher. Setz dafür vor dem Start zwei Umgebungsvariablen:

| Variable | Einstellung | Wert |
| -------- | ----------- | ---- |
| `OBJECT_STORAGE_BACKEND` | `storage.backend` | `filesystem` (Standard: `s3`) |
| `OBJECT_STORAGE_ROOT` | `storage.filesystem.root` | absoluter Ordner, zum Beispiel `<App-Daten>/local/<Arbeitsbereich>/files` |

Beide Werte gelten nur beim Start. Eine gespeicherte Revision ändert sie nicht, und die Settings-APIs lehnen Änderungen ab. Die Werte unter `storage.object_store` brauchst du in diesem Modus nicht.

- **Prüfung beim Start:** Der übergeordnete Ordner muss existieren. Die Engine legt den Ordner mit Modus `0700` an, setzt einen vorhandenen auf `0700` und prüft, dass sie darin schreiben, lesen, löschen und Hard-Links anlegen kann. Schlägt eine Prüfung fehl, startet die Engine nicht und nennt Grund und Abhilfe (`root_parent_missing`, `root_not_directory`, `root_not_writable`, `root_cross_device`, `root_no_hard_links`).
- **Schreiben:** Jedes Objekt landet erst in einer Zwischendatei, wird auf die Platte geschrieben und dann an seinen Platz verlinkt. Wer liest, sieht das ganze Objekt oder keins. Ein vorhandener Schlüssel wird nie überschrieben. Dateien bekommen Modus `0600`, Ordner `0700`.
- **Schlüssel:** Jedes Segment wird in kleine ASCII-Zeichen übersetzt (`a-z`, `0-9`, `.`, `_`, `-`, alles andere als `%xx`). So bleiben Schlüssel getrennt, die sich nur in Groß- und Kleinschreibung oder Unicode-Form unterscheiden, auch auf Platten ohne Unterscheidung der Schreibweise. Reservierte Windows-Namen sind sicher. `..`, leere Segmente und absolute Schlüssel lehnt die Engine ab, und einem Link aus dem Ordner hinaus folgt sie nie.
- **Sicherung:** Der Ordner ist der ganze Objektspeicher. Kopier ihn zusammen mit dem Datenbank-Dump.
- **Nicht unterstützt:** Netzlaufwerke, Ordner mit Cloud-Sync und Platten ohne Hard-Links wie exFAT.

Name, Zeitzone und Sprache eines Arbeitsbereichs sind keine Laufzeiteinstellungen. Du änderst sie in den Einstellungen unter Arbeitsbereich oder mit `PATCH /v1/identity/workspace`. Die Sprache gilt für Texte, für die keine Person ihre eigene Sprache mitbringt, etwa Gerätenamen und geplante Aufgaben; Standard ist Englisch.

Die Referenz unten wird aus der Konfiguration erzeugt und ist deshalb auf Englisch.

# SubKit runtime settings

Look up every runtime setting with its description and default value.
You change a value with `subkit settings configure` and `subkit settings set`, through the
HTTP or MCP settings APIs, or in the canonical config file. Per-tenant overrides go
into the file's `tenants` section and only apply to settings tagged `scope=tenant`.

A value resolves in this order: tenant overlay, then global value, then schema
default. Environment variables never set a runtime setting; only the bootstrap-only
process bindings `database.url`, `storage.backend`, `storage.filesystem.root` and
`deployment.mode` (from `SUBKIT_DEPLOYMENT_MODE`) come from the environment at startup.
